read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of reader/data/route-store of the main branch at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4 (its index.json), for "MACULA exact Hebrew morph surfaces with Cherith English definitions" (M3): 43,304 routes (axis: routes), 15,871 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row equals the route text on 43,304 of the routes. The source audit: each route's store record names one line of the lane's copy of the source file macula-hebrew.tsv (Clear-Bible/macula-hebrew at commit 47db250bd55d, in ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/macula-hebrew-2026-07-15/); the record's text equals that line's english column on 43,304 of 43,304 records (axis: records), and the route joins its record on 43,303 routes exactly and on 1 once a double space is closed (axis: routes). That column is the one field a route comes from, so no test here stands on a guess about a field; the audit is evidence about the source and no part of any test. The source's own key to its signs: none found. The lane's copy holds the licence page, which names the English as Cherith's glosses and points to a folder sources/Cherith/glosses that the copy does not hold, a page on how the TSV is generated, the lane's own manifests and extracts, the record of the source's commit, and the TSV itself; none of them gives an account of the sign ~, of round brackets, or of the signs =, +, /, full stop, ! and ?. So every shape whose meaning says what one of those signs is for begins "unverified:", and that is every shape but the curly apostrophe's and hyphen.between_two_letters, which are plain English spelling and say only that. Fetching the source's gloss folder needs the owner's word and was not done.

definitions.terms: In every test a character is one Unicode code point (every route holds only characters of 16 bits). A letter is any character of Unicode category L (JavaScript \p{L}). A digit is one of 0 to 9. A space is the character U+0020 only, and no test uses whitespace of any other kind. Nothing is trimmed: the text is the whole route text as it stands, which is the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def; the text before and the text after the mark are the template's c.before and c.after, and what a bracket holds is the template's c.group, the same for an opener and for its closer. An opener that never closes has a c.group of null and a closer that never opened has an empty one: no test here reads such a bracket, so classify throws there, and no route holds one. Directly before and directly after name the one character next to the mark or next to the named string; where the mark or the string stands at that end of the text no character stands there, so a test that asks for a character there fails, and a test that says if there is one passes. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it. Every string and every list minds case and is matched exact to the character, so «s» is the lowercase letter and «S» the uppercase one. Contains means a plain search for the run of characters anywhere in the thing the test names, with no word boundary: a test on what a bracket holds searches what the bracket holds and not the whole text, and a test on the text searches the whole text. Begins with, said of what a bracket holds, speaks of its first character.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence, and no later shape is tried for it. Not caught above means that no earlier shape of the same mark took the occurrence. A shape's container field is not part of its test: a test looks at the container only where its words say so, and the checker compares the field afterwards.

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number: a number in round brackets after a part of a name is a pointer to the whole name, never identity. The source's own file fills, over its 475,911 rows (axis: rows), an id (xml:id) on 475,911, a number (strongnumberx) on 475,911, a lemma (lemma) on 475,911 and a sense number (sensenumber) on 180,502; the route store carries none of them, and the dictionary store's record keeps only the line and the id of one cited place. The letters key here is a word form and its routes are the source's renderings of that form at its places, identical ones collapsed, so keys_with_more_than_one_route_text counts renderings at places, not entries. By the audit, which reads the one place each route's record cites, of the 7,227 such keys (axis: keys) 5,006 are keys whose routes cite one number of the source and 2,221 are keys whose routes cite two or more, so that the texts come from different words that share the letters (example key ו, whose routes cite 2050b, 2050c, 2050d).
